[[File:MarcoSturm2018.jpg|thumb|Marco Sturm is currently serving as head coach of the Bruins, being hired in 2025]]
{{Short description|None}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2024}}
The [[Boston Bruins]], a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Boston]], has had 29 [[head coach]]es in its team history.<ref name="History">{{cite web|url=http://bruins.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=5489 |title=Boston Bruins – History |access-date=2008-06-29 |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080501130542/http://bruins.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=5489 |archive-date=2008-05-01 }}</ref> The franchise is a member of the [[Atlantic Division (NHL)|Atlantic Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). The franchise was founded in 1924 and entered the NHL as the first American-based expansion team, playing its initial seasons at the still-active [[Boston Arena]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gonu.com/sports/2010/1/28/matthewsarena.aspx?id=204 |title=Northeastern University Athletics Official Website |publisher=Gonu.com |access-date=March 18, 2011 |archive-date=December 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205024756/http://gonu.com/sports/2010/1/28/matthewsarena.aspx?id=204 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="fitz">{{cite web |author=Katy Fitzpatrick |url=http://www.uscho.com/news/college-hockey/id,17170/NUHuskieslookingforwardtorenovatedArenanewseason.html |title="New Season Brings Renovated Arena for Northeastern," ''USCHO.com'', October 2, 2009 |publisher=Uscho.com |date=October 2, 2009 |access-date=March 18, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100109213027/http://www.uscho.com/news/college-hockey/id,17170/NUHuskieslookingforwardtorenovatedArenanewseason.html |archive-date=January 9, 2010 }}</ref> It is an [[Original Six]] team, along with the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]], [[Detroit Red Wings]], [[New York Rangers]], [[Montreal Canadiens]] and [[Chicago Blackhawks]].<ref name="History"/> Its home arena is the 17,565-person capacity [[TD Garden]], where it has played since 1995, after leaving the [[Boston Garden]].<ref name="History"/>

[[Art Ross]] served three terms as the Bruins head coach.<ref name="Art"/> Ross, [[Lynn Patrick]], and [[Milt Schmidt]] have all been inducted to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]]. [[Harry Sinden]], [[Gerry Cheevers]], [[Tom Johnson (ice hockey)|Tom Johnson]] and [[Frank Patrick (ice hockey)|Frank Patrick]] are Hockey Hall of Fame inductees, and spent their entire coaching careers with the Bruins. [[Cooney Weiland]], [[Dit Clapper]], [[Terry O'Reilly]], [[Steve Kasper]] and [[Mike O'Connell]] also coached only for the Bruins,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|title=List of honored Builders|access-date=2008-01-05|publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528120538/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|archive-date=2009-05-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Official|title=List of honored Officials|access-date=2008-01-05|publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930080933/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Official|archive-date=2007-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Player|title=List of honored Players|access-date=2008-01-05|publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218151041/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Player|archive-date=2009-02-18}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Player|title=List of honored Players by Position|access-date=2008-01-06|publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218151041/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Player|archive-date=2009-02-18}}</ref><ref name="Sullivan"/> with [[Mike Sullivan (ice hockey)|Mike Sullivan]] taking over as head coach for the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] on December 12, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=792341 |title=Penguins fire Johnston, name Sullivan coach |last1=Crosby |first1=Wes |date=December 12, 2015 |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=December 12, 2015 |quote=The Pittsburgh Penguins on Saturday fired coach Mike Johnston and replaced him with Mike Sullivan. |archive-date=December 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151213213406/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=792341 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Statistically, Tom Johnson was the most successful head coach, with a winning percentage of .738.<ref name="Johnson"/> He is followed by [[Harry Sinden]], who, averaging his two terms, had a winning percentage of .689.<ref name="Harry"/> The worst head coach statistically was [[Phil Watson]], who, with a winning percentage of .268, only won 16 out of the 84 games he coached.<ref name="Watson"/> [[Claude Julien (ice hockey)|Claude Julien]] took over after [[Dave Lewis (ice hockey)|Dave Lewis]] was dismissed in 2007.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/dave-lewis-ousted-as-bruins-coach-1.643587 |title=Dave Lewis ousted as Bruins coach |access-date=2008-06-29 |date=2007-06-15 |work=CBC Sports |publisher=cbc.ca |archive-date=2012-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102122536/http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/story/2007/06/15/lewis-bruins-nhl.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Julien"/> [[Bruce Cassidy]] succeeded Julien on February 7, 2017, and served as head coach until his firing on June 6, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bruins Relieve Bruce Cassidy Of Coaching Duties |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/bruins-relieve-bruce-cassidy-of-coaching-duties-334507330 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 8, 2022 |date=June 6, 2022 |archive-date=June 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220606231920/https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/bruins-relieve-bruce-cassidy-of-coaching-duties/c-334507330 |url-status=live }}</ref> On June 30, 2022, the Bruins named [[Jim Montgomery (ice hockey)|Jim Montgomery]] head coach, replacing Cassidy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-01 |title=Jim Montgomery Named 29th Head Coach Of The Boston Bruins {{!}} Boston Bruins |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/jim-montgomery-named-29th-head-coach-of-the-boston-bruins-334794392 |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en |archive-date=2024-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240518042101/https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/jim-montgomery-named-29th-head-coach-of-the-boston-bruins-334794392 |url-status=live }}</ref> Following an 8–9–3 start to the [[2024–25 NHL season|2024–25 season]], Montgomery was fired, and replaced on an interim basis by assistant coach [[Joe Sacco (ice hockey)|Joe Sacco]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Amalie |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jim-montgomery-fired-as-boston-coach |title=Montgomery fired as Bruins coach, replaced by Sacco |website=NHL.com |date=November 19, 2024 |access-date=November 19, 2024}}</ref> On June 5, 2025, the Bruins announced that they had hired former player [[Marco Sturm]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marco Sturm Named 30th Head Coach in Boston Bruins History |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/marco-sturm-named-30th-head-coach-in-boston-bruins-history |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 5, 2025 |date=June 5, 2025}}</ref> Sturm is the first European coach in franchise history, being from Germany.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}}
